audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0..6].side read "Skill" on every row while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Skill, Skill, Skill, Ahri, Ahri, Ahri, Ahri.
audit.why: Ahri holds 53.97% over 1825 games and takes over from levels 4-5 onward; the page was rendering two different answers to the same four rows.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side flipped to Ahri as one group, matching win[3..6] which were already Ahri.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was attributed to "Blooming Burst" in spikes[1], whys[4], mid and wants.you[2].
audit.why: Blooming Burst is Neeko's Q — a 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 second poke seed she has had since level 1. Her level 6 ability is Pop Blossom (R), 120/105/90 seconds. Every sentence about the 6 spike was pointing at the wrong ability, and the advice built on it ("punish her after Blooming Burst goes on cooldown post-6") was therefore worthless.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten around Pop Blossom and its 120-second rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were wrong or absent. (a) The page repeatedly said to sidestep Tangle-Barbs "behind minions". (b) Nothing anywhere stated that Charm breaks Inherent Glamour.
audit.why: (a) Riot's Tangle-Barbs text: it roots everything it passes through, and if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion it becomes larger, faster and roots for longer. Minions do not block it — feeding it a minion kill upgrades the root that then hits you. Standing behind the wave is actively worse than stepping sideways. (b) Inherent Glamour: receiving immobilizing crowd control breaks the disguise. Charm is immobilizing crowd control, so a landed charm strips the disguise outright — and Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden only while she is disguised.
audit.corrected: Minion-blocking advice replaced with lateral sidestepping in dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; the charm-breaks-disguise interaction added to whys[3] and spikes[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Pop Blossom's hidden wind-up while disguised was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's own R text ends "The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised" — that is the single most punishing hidden mechanic in the matchup and it decides whether your last Spirit Rush dash is banked or spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neeko was written as "his"/"he" throughout the full layer, and dosFull[2].d cited a "fifteen-second" Tangle-Barbs cooldown.
audit.why: Neeko is female, and Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 — never fifteen. A fabricated cooldown is worse than a vague one because a player will time a step-up on it.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the cooldown corrected to its real 12 seconds.

notes: Two substantive factual errors, both of which would have made a player misplay: Blooming Burst (her Q) was named as the level 6 power spike in four places when the spike is Pop Blossom (R, 120s), and the page told the reader four separate times to sidestep Tangle-Barbs 'behind minions' when Riot's own text says it roots everything it passes through and gets larger, faster and longer-rooting if it kills a unit — hiding in the wave upgrades the root that hits you. Also corrected: a fabricated 'fifteen-second' Tangle-Barbs cooldown (real: 12/11.5/11/10.5/10) and male pronouns throughout. Level chart disagreed between layers on rows 4-7. Not asserted, because the kit cannot answer it: whether Charm interrupts Pop Blossom's preparation once the leap has started (Charm stops movement abilities and the R carries a dash flag, but Riot's text does not say the prep is interruptible), and whether Charm is cleansable or tenacity-reduced.
